name: Freelance crowd software tester (uTest / Applause)
summary: Free-to-join tester community where you accept paid invitations to find bugs and run test cases on clients' apps and websites.
whatYouDo: After building a profile with your devices and finishing an introductory Sandbox/Academy cycle, you receive invitations matched to your profile. You test apps or sites, report bugs or run test cases, and are paid once the client approves your work.
appeal: Free to sign up; run by established testing company Applause
Payout is shown before you accept an invitation
Paid twice a month (15th and month-end) via PayPal or Payoneer
Builds hands-on QA skills that can lead to software-testing jobs
watchOuts: Many testers report few or no paid invitations, especially at first; invitations depend on rating, devices and country
You are paid only for approved bugs/tasks; rejected work earns nothing
Canada eligibility not stated on an official page we could see

training.notes: Introductory Sandbox class and uTest Academy courses; practice cycles are unpaid.

compensation.notes: Pay per approved bug, test case or project; amount shown per invitation. A review blog cites ~$3–100 per approved bug by severity (unverified).

reliability.notes: r/UTEST threads (2023–2025) report few invitations even after Academy work; a 2026 review says projects are not guaranteed.

applicationSteps: Create a free uTest profile listing your devices
Link a PayPal or Payoneer account
Accept paid invitations as they arrive
fitsIf: You are detail-oriented, own several devices, and want to learn software testing while earning occasionally.
